column1: # ci/red-arms/batch16-spotcheck.tsv -- TEXTUAL spot-checks for #289 batch 16.
# Feed to:  bash ci/pump-red-arm.sh linux-clang-debug ci/red-arms/batch16-spotcheck.tsv
# The stronger witness. `ci/red-arms/batch16-labels.txt` runs all 49 sites through the
# runtime seam in one build; these six rebuild the tree once PER ARM with the miss
# forced textually, so they check the recipe as WRITTEN rather than as the seam
# reports it. Run both.
# ⚠️ EVERY ROW CARRIES SIX FIELDS, AND COLUMN 6 IS LOAD-BEARING HERE.
# file <TAB> anchor <TAB> label <TAB> cmake-target <TAB> ctest-regex <TAB> exec-stem
# A label matches EXACTLY at the forcing seam but by CONTAINMENT for the driver's
# "did this arm's own test run?" assertion, and those two coincide only while labels
# are named after TESTS. Four of these six sites live in fixture HELPERS reached from
# many tests, so without column 6 they would every one read INCONCLUSIVE for a reason
# about naming rather than about the site. Column 6 names the gtest SUITE.
# ⚠️ AND SAY WHAT COLUMN 6 DOES NOT PROVE: a suite name shows the SUITE ran, not that
# the armed site was reached. A site no executed test calls would grade SILENT (a
# finding about the site) rather than INCONCLUSIVE. That gap is recorded as open
# #289 work in the batch-15 handover; it is not closed here.
# ⚠️ ANCHOR ON THE SITE, NOT ON WHAT ENCLOSES IT -- UNLESS THE LABEL NAMES THE
# ENCLOSING FUNCTION'S FIRST SITE. The driver forces the FIRST `run_window_then_ready(`
# at or after the anchor, so a signature anchor on a two-site helper forces site one and
# reports about site two. That cost batch 15 a wrong verdict against correct code. The
# three signature anchors below are each a helper's FIRST site, checked; the other
# three anchor on the `co_spawn` immediately above their own call.
# ⚠️ AN ANCHOR MUST BE UNIQUE IN ITS FILE, and that is not free here: the two shared
# helpers below both spawn `sess.open()`, and that exact line recurs in the same file.
# Re-derive rather than trusting these strings after an edit:
#   grep -cF '<anchor>' <file>      # must print 1
# ⚠️ `PossDupTestBase::drive_to_active/open` LIVES IN A SHARED HEADER compiled into
# four binaries. Its arm targets ONE of them on purpose (session_inbound_poss_resend):
# the mutation is textual and rebuilds every includer, so a broader ctest regex would
# multiply the arm's cost without adding a witness -- the same source line is under
# test either way. That the OTHER three includers still build and pass with the
# mutation reverted is what the full suite run covers, not this arm.
